title: Chapter 283: Sister Is Behind That Man
html:
“Fan Yu told other children weird things?”

Chen Ge immediately grasped the source of the problem. Fan Yu could see ghosts. The boy was not malicious, and although his words might sound bizarre to adults, they were probably true.

“Yes. To keep him from disrupting the other children’s treatment, we had to send several of them to a child psychiatrist for counseling. You must understand that we’re a public institution with a limited budget. Much of our operation depends on charitable donations.” The director sighed. “We can afford an occasional appointment, but not if this continues.”

He studied Chen Ge, trying to gauge his response. Seeing him deep in thought, the director assumed he understood the implication and relaxed slightly. “Given Fan Yu’s condition, his chances of adoption are low. Since you’re his only family, I believe he would be better off living with you than remaining at the Children’s Home.”

The room fell into silence.

After two minutes of silence, Chen Ge reached a conclusion. “Fan Yu hasn’t done anything wrong.”

The director blinked, wondering whether he had failed to explain himself. “I know this isn’t Fan Yu’s fault. We only want him to grow up healthy, so please don’t misunderstand.”

“What exactly did Fan Yu tell them?” Chen Ge regarded the director gravely. “I need every word. Those children may be in danger.”

“Danger?” The director stared at him for three full seconds, mouth hanging open. His carefully prepared speech had become useless; they were not remotely on the same wavelength. Looking at Chen Ge, he suddenly wondered whether Fan Yu’s condition might be hereditary.

“Yes, please tell me what Fan Yu has said and the names and contact information of those children. They might be in serious danger,” Chen Ge repeated seriously; it did not sound like he was kidding.

The director forced a smile. “Mr. Chen, I’ll be blunt. Fan Yu feels no sense of belonging here; he probably wants to live with his family. He’s extremely intelligent, but he has serious psychological problems. If you can afford it, we hope you’ll take him home and arrange treatment with a qualified child psychiatrist.”

“That isn’t possible right now. My home isn’t safe.” Chen Ge was telling the truth. Until the Ghost Stories Society had been eliminated, he could not bring Fan Yu to the Haunted House.

The director had heard countless excuses from people reluctant to adopt, but personal safety was a new one. “Very well, but you must visit and speak with him often. We’ll continue doing everything we can.”

“Thank you.”

The nurse escorted Chen Ge from the director’s office. Looking embarrassed, she said, “We aren’t trying to drive Fan Yu away. He’s obedient and intelligent; he simply does unusual things.”

Chen Ge smiled but did not argue. “I know what you’re trying to express, but have you considered that what he says is the truth?”

The nurse slowed and glanced at him. For some reason, his certainty made him strangely convincing. “We’re here.”

She stopped beside the room where they had encountered the two boys earlier. Both doors stood open. “Jiang He and Jiang Jin have run off again.”

She hurried into one room. Glass shattered in the bedroom, followed by a little girl’s anguished cry. “Big Sister!”

It sounded like her sister was being bullied.

“Jiang Jin, Jiang He! Go stand facing the wall!” As the nurse scolded the two boys, Chen Ge paused in the doorway. On the painted name card, Fan Yu’s name stood out among those of all the children surnamed Jiang.

This boy certainly knows how to make people worry.Chen Ge entered the bedroom. Fan Yu sat at a table, head bowed over a drawing and utterly detached from the commotion around him. Beside him, a little girl sobbed uncontrollably. She scrubbed at her eyes with tiny hands, but the tears kept falling as she called for her sister.

After dealing with Jiang Jin and Jiang He, the nurse gathered the girl into her arms, but the child only cried harder. Her tearful eyes reddened as she pointed at the boys. “They killed Sister! They killed my big sister!”

Bundled in thick clothing, the adorable girl resembled a ball of cotton in the nurse’s arms. Yet words of killing and murder continued spilling from her small lips.

“Jiang Jin, Jiang He! What have you two done?!” The nurse was angry, feeling pity for the little girl.

“We only wanted to look at her glass jar, but she wouldn’t let us. It broke by accident, and then someone accidentally stepped on the spider inside,” the boys muttered resentfully.

“Spider? Big sister?” Chen Ge turned to look at the center of the bedroom. The glass cup was shattered, and amid the broken pieces, there was a flattened spider.

Once the nurse understood what had happened, she sent the boys from the room and tried to comfort the girl. The child would not listen. Sobbing even harder, she wriggled free, picked the crushed spider from the floor, and cradled it in her palms without revulsion. She ran to Fan Yu and wailed despairingly, “They killed Sister! Big Sister is dead!”

The girl appeared no older than four or five. Even on tiptoe, she barely rose above the tabletop. Fan Yu remained absorbed in his drawing and ignored her.

Eventually, however, her crying exhausted his patience. He set down his pencil and rested a hand on her head. “Sister isn’t dead. She only left for a little while.”

Fan Yu used his other hand to pick up the picture and showed it to the girl. “Your sister was just behind you.”

On the plain sheet, a black pencil depicted a tightly bound little girl. Behind her, drawn in red, crouched an enormous humanoid monster.

It loomed over the child, its elongated head resting atop hers and its limbs splayed across the ground like a spider’s. At the sight of Fan Yu’s drawing, the little girl finally stopped crying.

Fan Yu ruffled the girl’s hair, then looked toward Chen Ge in the doorway. “See? Sister is standing behind that man now.”
